The applicant has filed this second application u/S.438 Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.
His first application for the same relief was dismissed on merits vide order dated 2.5.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.18555/2023.
T h e applicant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.81/2023 registered at Police Station Unnao, District Datia (M.P.) fo r the offence punishable under Sections 409 and 420 of IPC.

A s per prosecution story complainant Harish Prajapati, Panchayat Co- ordination Officer, Janpad Datia filed a complaint before concerning Police Station to the effect that the Gram Rojgar Sahayak of Village Rajapur has not deposited the amount of wages of the beneficiaries of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojna in their account and deposited the amount to the accounts of other labourers.

In regard to that complaint received and inquiry was done by complainant and B.C. (Residential) in which payment of 90 days wages has not been made in the beneficiaries' account. In such circumstances,

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant-accused argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
The applicant has not committed any offence.
He has been falsely implicated in the case without conducting any inquiry.

In earlier bail application it could not be submitted that amount was passed by Panchayat Co-ordinator and Muster roll is to be issued by Chief Executive Officer,
Janpad; therefore, present application is maintainable.
The applicant is permanent resident of District Datia.

He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by the Court; therefore, it has been prayed that this second application be allowed and applicant be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

O n the other hand, learned State counsel has vehemently opposed the bail application by submitting that first application for the same relief filed by the present applicant has already been dismissed on merits and thereafter, the applicant was failed to show any change in circumstances.
It is further argued that there is sufficient material available on record to show the involvement of the applicant in the alleged crime.
It is further argued that after holding an inquiry, the applicant is found to be liable for commission of crime; therefore, active role in the commission of crime is apparent.
It is further argued that there is no weight in the argument of learned counsel for the applicant because the FIR is lodged after holding an inquiry in which the applicant is found guilty.
In such circumstances, the applicant should not be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Having heard the arguements of learned counsel for the parties and perusal of case diary, this Court finds that this is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Consequently, this second application for anticipatory bail is also hereby dismissed.
